 Not a single Kolkata AQI station records ‘good’ air; cracker fears mount

 Subhajoy Roy / Nov 07, 2026, 21:04 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Smoggy weather in Kolkata Kolkata: None of the seven air quality monitoring stations in Kolkata reported “good” or “satisfactory” readings, the two best readings, for much of Saturday. Two stations — at Jadavpur and Bidhannagar — reported “poor” air quality, which can lead to “breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure”. Green activists and scientists apprehend that if crackers are burst indiscriminately around Kali Puja-Diwali, the accumulated mass of particulate matter emitted by the crackers will further deteriorate the air quality. As winter approaches, wind speed slows down and rains dry up. The pollutants remain in the air for a longer duration. “Moderate” air quality was reported by the monitoring stations at Ballygunge, Fort William, Rabindra Bharati University, Rabindra Sarobar and Victoria. According to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), moderate air quality can cause breathing discomfort to the people with lungs, asthma and heart diseases. “The fall in mercury is directly related to increase in air pollution. With the fall in temperature, the air near the ground does not rise as fast as summer. As a result, the pollutants released into the air during winter remains in the air we breathe for a much longer duration,” said a scientist with the state pollution control board. “In summer, the load of pollutants released every day is possibly of the same volume. But as the warm air rises faster, it carries away the pollutants. Wind speed is higher in summer, which also helps in dissipating the pollutants,” said the scientist. PCB officials said a sudden surge in the load of pollutants, which can happen if there is indiscriminate bursting of crackers during Diwali, adds to the already bad air quality, if other climatological factors remain unchanged. “The crackers release huge quantities of pollutants. PM 10 and PM 2.5 concentration in the air goes up manifold if crackers are burst over a large area,” said an air quality management expert. Some of the crackers — the light-emitting ones — also contain heavy metals. Once they are burst, the heavy metals are released into the air. PCB sources said tailpipe emissions, dust generated, industrial emissions, construction activities and open burning of waste are among the top contributors to air pollution. Anumita Roy Chowdhury, executive director at the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE), said it was time to “limit pollution at the source”. “Pollution levels begin to build up from now. If the efforts to curb pollution are not taken around the year, extra efforts are needed in winter,” said Roy Chowdhury.
